\pagesubtitle{Piano \quad shown in C, move them anywhere}

\begin{rootmapnote}
A shell is the chord with its fifth taken out. The fifth says nothing about the chord, and leaving it out gets the third and the seventh, the two notes that do, under one hand.\\
The ninth chords go further and drop the root as well: the bass has it. Third, seventh, ninth is the whole sound.\\
For inversions, take whichever one moves least from the chord before it. Holding a common tone and stepping the rest is what makes a progression sound joined up rather than jumped between.
\end{rootmapnote}

\begin{rootmapnote}
Read across: in the key on the left, the four chord is the column headed 4. Call a song in numbers and it transposes itself.
